schema_query: Do federal judges appointed by different Presidents (Trump vs. other Republican vs. Democratic) differ in their voting tendencies on immigration injunction cases? Do Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration immigration policies compared to judges appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents?

columns.name: judge_name
columns.definition: The full name of the federal judge presiding over the case.
columns.rationale: Required to identify the specific judge and subsequently determine their appointing president.

columns.name: appointing_president
columns.definition: The U.S. President who appointed the judge to the federal bench.
columns.rationale: Directly addresses the core query comparing Trump appointees, other Republican appointees, and Democratic appointees.

columns.name: appointing_president_party
columns.definition: The political party of the President who appointed the judge.
columns.rationale: Allows grouping of judges to compare voting tendencies across party lines (Democratic vs. Republican).

columns.name: ruling_type
columns.definition: The type of ruling or decision issued by the judge in the case.
columns.rationale: Identifies whether the decision is a preliminary injunction, temporary restraining order, or other form of relief.

columns.name: ruling_outcome
columns.definition: The outcome of the ruling with respect to the challenged immigration policy.
columns.rationale: Determines whether the judge's vote supported or blocked the administration's policy, which is essential for analyzing voting tendencies.

columns.name: challenged_policy_administration
columns.definition: The presidential administration that enacted the challenged immigration policy.
columns.rationale: Allows researchers to evaluate if judges are more or less supportive of policies enacted by specific administrations (e.g., the Trump administration).
